instruction: Implement `pub fn eval(expr: &str) -> Result<i64, String>` in this file, replacing the stub. It evaluates a space-separated reverse-Polish-notation (postfix) integer expression. Each token is either an integer or one of the operators + - * / which pop two operands (first popped is b, second is a) and compute a OP b, pushing the result. Return Ok(value) when exactly one value remains on the stack at the end. Return Err(...) on any of: division by zero; an operator applied with fewer than two operands available; a token that is neither an operator nor a parseable integer; or a final stack whose length is not exactly 1. Examples: eval("3 4 +")=Ok(7), eval("5 1 2 + 4 * + 3 -")=Ok(14), eval("42")=Ok(42), eval("10 2 /")=Ok(5), eval("1 0 /")=Err, eval("1 +")=Err, eval("1 2 x")=Err. Edit only this file.
